stories.label: Deadly fire breaks out at Canada military base
stories.summary: A fire tore through Canadian Forces Base Wainwright in Alberta, killing and injuring an as-yet-uncounted number of people; Defence Minister David McGuinty called it 'very tragic' but would not give a toll or a cause. Lead with what is known and what officials are withholding — casualties, what the base houses and trains for, and whether this was an accident or an incident. Dateline Wainwright.

stories.label: Marco Rubio says Trump's Russian oil sanctions waiver is a '60-day pause,' denies restricting Starlink access
stories.summary: New development on the sanctions-waiver arc: Rubio now puts a clock on it — a '60-day pause' on sanctions against Russian oil sales — and denies Washington is throttling Ukraine's Starlink access, while Zelenskyy floats a US-Russia-Ukraine meeting at the G20. Lead with the 60 days: who buys Russian crude in that window (India, Turkey, China) and what it does to Brent crude, then the leverage question — sanctions relief offered before any ceasefire term is fixed.

stories.label: US ambassador urges Israel to prosecute attackers of American journalist
stories.summary: Settlers attacked Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine in the occupied West Bank — she needed surgery on a nearly severed finger — and even Mike Huckabee, Washington's most settler-friendly ambassador, called it terror and demanded jail. New development on the West Bank arc after Taybeh. Lead with the accountability gap: Israel rarely prosecutes settler violence against Palestinians; the test is whether a US citizen's case changes that, and what it says that it takes one.

stories.label: Why are people protesting in Milan?
stories.summary: Cost-of-living protests have spread from France to Italy: police fired tear gas at stone-throwing crowds outside Milan's cathedral and clashed with marchers in Bologna and Turin, with the CGIL union behind the mobilisation and Meloni condemning the violence. Lead with what is squeezing Italian households — energy and food prices since the Hormuz war, wages — and the mechanism linking a Gulf war to European streets.

stories.label: Hormuz insecurity result of US, Israeli aggression: Araghchi
stories.summary: New development in the Gulf war: Araghchi says Iran has put a concrete proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, while blaming the insecurity on the US-Israeli war that began 28 February; Russia's Alexander Novak warns emergency oil stockpiles are nearly exhausted, so prices rise further if Hormuz is not settled. Lead with the proposal's terms as far as known, and tie it to Brent crude and ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian and Russian claims must be attributed.

stories.label: Bacteroides-Escherichia interactions contribute to colonization resistance against Clostridioides difficile
stories.summary: C. difficile is a leading cause of hospital-acquired infection, usually after antibiotics wipe out gut flora. This study finds that two ordinary gut commensals, Bacteroides and E. coli, together block its colonisation — a mechanism that could guide defined bacterial therapies to replace crude faecal transplants. Lead with the interaction and what it means for patients after antibiotics.

stories.label: World's oldest shipwreck discovered off coast of Turkey
stories.summary: Archaeologists tentatively date a wreck off Turkey's coast to 2700–2400 BC from its pottery cargo, which would make it the oldest known shipwreck. Lead with the date and how it was reached from cargo alone, since almost nothing of the hull survives; then what it says about Early Bronze Age Aegean–Anatolian sea trade.

stories.label: Huggingface发榜，中国模型StartLux稳居决策模型SOTA
stories.summary: A Chinese model, StartLux, tops a Hugging Face leaderboard for 'decision models' — the small controller that routes an agent's tasks, manages compute cost and states its uncertainty. Lead with what the benchmark measures and the claimed result, and why the inside view from China's tech press frames the agent era as a contest for this layer rather than for the largest model. Attribute the ranking claims.

stories.label: Here's What Consumer Reports Found Out When It Looked Into Uber's AI Rideshare Pricing - AOL
stories.summary: Consumer Reports investigated how Uber's AI pricing sets fares. Lead with the finding — whether riders are charged different prices for the same trip based on data about them — and the accountability gap: algorithmic personalised pricing that no regulator audits. Name what Uber disclosed and what it would not.

stories.label: VK data center in Leningrad Region targeted by drone attack
stories.summary: In a Ukrainian drone raid on St Petersburg and the Leningrad Region — 126 drones downed, per the governor — a data centre of VK, Russia's largest social network, was hit; VK says services stayed up. Lead with data centres becoming war targets, a week after Iran threatened Gulf AI data centres and subsea cables. Russian state-media claims must be attributed to TASS.

stories.label: Number of Ebola cases in Kenya rises to seven -- agency
stories.summary: New development since our 14 Oct story (second case): Kenya confirmed four more Bundibugyo Ebola cases, total seven, and three of them are health workers who treated the country's first patient. Lead with the health workers: infections inside the clinic mean infection control failed at the first point of contact, and Bundibugyo has no licensed vaccine. Note the DRC outbreak behind it (over 9,000 cases) and what Nairobi is doing on quarantine and contact tracing. Dateline Nairobi. TASS is one of three sources; Al Jazeera and TRT carry it independently.

stories.label: Turkish, Egyptian foreign ministers meet in Baghdad
stories.summary: Frame on the OIC's 52nd foreign ministers' session opening in Baghdad, with the Fidan–Abdelatty meeting as one thread: the Muslim world's main bloc convenes in an Iraqi capital with a Gulf war under way, Hormuz closed and Gaza goods halted. Lead with what the session is set to address and what, if anything, it can decide or enforce; Pakistan Observer reports Iraq praising Pakistan's peace efforts. Say plainly if no binding outcome is on the table. Dateline Baghdad.

stories.label: Pakistan suspends Iran trade corridors of Gabd-Rimdan, Taftan
stories.summary: Pakistan's commerce ministry withdrew, with immediate effect, its earlier order allowing trade with Iran through the Gabd-Rimdan and Taftan crossings — the official land corridors that carry Iranian LPG and goods into Balochistan. Lead with who pays: border traders and LPG-dependent households in Gwadar and Quetta, in a province already short of fuel and work, a week after weekly inflation hit 11%. Ask why now (the Gulf war, US sanctions pressure) and what it does to the informal fuel trade. Dateline Quetta.

stories.label: Trump Warns California Election Officials of Jail Time if They Let Noncitizens Vote
stories.summary: The DOJ warned California officials they will be criminally charged if they count mail-in ballots from some 200,000 people it flagged as potential noncitizens, and Trump promised jail. Lead with the mechanism: the federal government threatening prosecution of the state officials who certify a midterm count, weeks before the vote. Say how the 200,000 were identified and whether the list has been tested — flagged is not proven, and eligible voters can be caught in such matches. Attribute claims carefully; the source is partisan. Dateline Los Angeles.

stories.label: Yemeni government forces report killing 800 Houthis in past day
stories.summary: The internationally recognised Yemeni government's spokesman Majid al-Nuzaili claims its forces killed over 800 Houthi fighters in a day and took new ground on the eastern front. Advances our 10–15 Oct coverage of the push toward Bab el-Mandeb and the Houthi strikes on Aden. Must be attributed: Russian state news agency TASS relaying a combatant's figure, unverified and likely inflated — say so, and say what independent counts exist. Lead with what the claim, if near true, means for the Red Sea chokepoint and for civilians on the front.

stories.label: Police brutality at nationwide protests in France continues
stories.summary: Nationwide protests continued across France on Saturday, with demonstrators, largely young, trying to march on government buildings in Paris and clashing with police. Follows the 13 Oct student march over run-down schools. Lead with the facts the source can support — where, how many, arrests, injuries — and what the protesters demand. Must be attributed: Iranian state news agency Mehr reported it, and its 'brutality' framing cannot be stated as fact. Dateline Paris.

stories.label: Noise-cancelling headphones prevent vomiting after surgery | New Scientist
stories.summary: Patients who wore noise-cancelling headphones on the operating table, under general anaesthetic, were less likely to vomit after surgery. Lead with the surprise: the anaesthetised brain still processes operating-theatre noise, and that noise feeds nausea. Give the trial size and the size of the effect, and note what a near-free intervention means for hospitals that cannot afford anti-nausea drugs.

stories.label: 上下文争夺，为何成了办公AI新战场？
stories.summary: The inside view from China's tech press: office AI makers there are now fighting over context — who holds a company's internal chats, documents and customer records that agents need to work. Lead with the concrete moves and named platforms (DingTalk, Feishu, WeCom and others) the piece reports, and the mechanism: whoever owns the context locks in the customer. Stick to reported facts, not the outlet's forecasts. Dateline Beijing.

stories.label: West Bank: Israeli settlers attack EU diplomats, French mayor
stories.summary: New development on the olive-harvest attacks covered this morning: settlers beat French mayor Bernard Baudoux with iron bars and attacked EU diplomats on a goodwill visit to Taybeh, and France's prime minister says France will not be intimidated. Lead with the iron bars and the diplomatic status of the victims: if settlers attack European officials with impunity, the reader can measure what Palestinian villagers face daily. Name who has the power to stop it: the Israeli army and police in Area C.

stories.label: Kolkata Stampede: Visuals Show Massive Rush At Durga Puja Pandal
stories.summary: At least 17 dead and about 35 in hospital after a crush at the Sarada Park (Chor Bagan) Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata, in heavy rain and a packed crowd. Lead with the toll, then the accountability question Congress is already asking: who licensed the crowd size and where the police were. Note Modi's Rs 2 lakh ex gratia. This is a disaster story, filed as politics.

stories.label: Mexico surfers murder: three jailed for 158 years
stories.summary: A Baja California judge sentenced three men to more than 158 years each for killing Australian brothers Jake and Callum Robinson and American Carter Rhoad in a robbery. The angle is the contrast: a conviction in a country where most homicides never reach a verdict. Ask whether foreign victims get a justice system Mexican victims rarely see. Dateline Ensenada.

stories.label: Coastal homes burn as hot winds fuel California wildfires
stories.summary: The Norte fire near San Juan Capistrano and San Clemente, driven by Santa Ana winds, burned at least six coastal homes and forced thousands to evacuate, with fire weather lasting through Saturday night. Lead with the October timing: a fire season that no longer ends. Name what the late heat means for insurers pulling out of California. A disaster, filed as politics.

stories.label: Ilhan Omar's lawyers demand the return of property seized in house raid
stories.summary: Lawyers for Rep. Ilhan Omar, the first Somali-American and one of two Muslim women in Congress, demand the return of property federal agents seized from her Washington home. They say the search broke the Speech or Debate safeguards that protect members of Congress. Lead with the precedent: the Justice Department searching a sitting opposition lawmaker's home. Explain the constitutional shield and what it covers.

stories.label: Trump's ballroom blitz: Leaked donor list reveals Apple, Nvidia gave $25M each -- but the president's name is missing - AOL
stories.summary: A leaked donor list for the White House ballroom names the backers of $330 million, including $25M each from Apple and Nvidia, two companies whose export licences and tariffs the administration decides. Trump's own promised contribution is not on it. Lead with the two $25M lines next to the decisions pending before the White House: this is the conflict-of-interest mechanism in one table.

stories.label: Nigeria drove thousands of gold miners from a national park. But can it keep them out?
stories.summary: A military-backed operation drove more than 4,000 illegal gold miners out of Gashaka-Gumti, Nigeria's largest national park and a refuge for the endangered Nigeria-Cameroon chimpanzee. The parks chief admits the miners may come back. Lead with the 4,000, then the mechanism: miners with no other livelihood, gold buyers who stay out of reach, and a park too big to guard. Dateline Gashaka-Gumti or the nearest town the source names.

stories.label: Mental health group welcomes Senate move to decriminalise attempted suicide
stories.summary: Nigeria's Senate passed the Suicide Prevention Bill (SB 730), which repeals the colonial-era law that made attempted suicide a crime punishable by prison. The vote is the news, not the advocacy group's welcome. Lead with what changes for people who survive an attempt: they go to treatment, not jail. Say which steps remain before it becomes law: the House and the president's assent.

stories.label: Albanian police use rubber bullets against protestors in Tirana -- CNA
stories.summary: New development in the protests covered on 15 October, when demonstrators burned the education ministry: on the fifth straight day, police in Tirana fired rubber bullets as protesters tried to seize government buildings. The only source is Russian state news agency TASS, citing Serbian outlet CNA, so attribute every claim and state nothing as fact. Explain the stakes: Rama's refusal to resign and Albania's 2028 EU accession target.

stories.label: Govt scrambles to solve fuel crisis without clear end in sight, divided on fava bean import ban; Quintet tries to balance competing political initiatives; RSF continues Blue Nile push; Military sets sights on Darfur
stories.summary: Sudan's wartime fuel crisis has turned petrol stations into campsites as prices soar, while the Port Sudan government publicly projects calm and argues internally over a ban on fava bean imports, the staple of the Sudanese breakfast. Lead with the queues and the price rise: two of the most basic goods of daily life are now in short supply at once. Use the RSF push in Blue Nile and the army's Darfur plans as context for why supply routes are breaking. Dateline Port Sudan.

stories.label: Indian airlines barred from using Pakistani airspace until Nov 24 as ban extended
stories.summary: Pakistan extended its ban on Indian-registered and Indian-operated aircraft for another month, to 24 November, by NOTAM. Lead with the cost: every India-to-Europe, Gulf and North America flight detours around Pakistan, adding fuel and hours, and Pakistan gives up overflight fees. The reader should see how a month-by-month renewal has made a wartime measure permanent. Dateline Karachi or Islamabad.

stories.label: Li Yuankun: Is the OECD Using the Right Benchmark for China's Subsidies?
stories.summary: A Chinese Academy of Social Sciences economist argues the OECD inflates China's industrial subsidy estimates by treating any borrowing below a market benchmark rate as a subsidy. That figure feeds the EU and US cases for tariffs and the anti-coercion tool. Lead with the mechanism: which interest rate counts as 'market' in an economy run by state banks decides whether China subsidises heavily or moderately. This is the Beijing view of a number Western trade policy rests on; present it as his argument.

stories.label: Persian Gulf Internet, AI Infrastructures within Iran's reach
stories.summary: Iran has warned that submarine internet cables and data centres in the Gulf could be targets if it is attacked again, widening the war onto the region's digital infrastructure: the Gulf's AI data-centre build-out and the cables that carry Europe-Asia traffic. The only source is Iranian state news agency Mehr: attribute the threat and do not state Iran's capability as fact. Explain why this matters to a technical reader: a handful of cable landing points and hyperscale sites that drone strikes have already disrupted (AWS Bahrain, March).

stories.label: Child, four women among Palestinians injured in West Bank pogroms
stories.summary: New since yesterday's beating of olive pickers and a Washington Post photographer: a prominent far-right rabbi issued a religious edict permitting settlers to seize Palestinian olives, and attacks spread across the West Bank — a child and four women injured — while Israeli forces arrested the farmers, not the attackers. Lead with the edict turning the harvest into licensed theft, and name who was hurt and who was detained.

stories.label: Latest vote shows no candidate for UN chief has the required support of all five key powers
stories.summary: In the Security Council's latest straw poll none of the seven candidates to succeed Guterres escaped a veto-holder's discouragement, and Senegal's former president Macky Sall has withdrawn. Lead with the mechanism: five states can quietly kill any candidate, so the world's top diplomat is chosen by the P5's mutual vetoes; note whether the Global South's candidates (Sall, Grynspan) are being squeezed out.

stories.label: 10 tourists killed in fire at Inani resort flagged as risky in June: Fire Service
stories.summary: Ten tourists died in a fire at the Tuptup Resort at Inani, Cox's Bazar — a resort the Fire Service had inspected and flagged as risky in June, and which operated with no fire approval at all. Lead with the four-month gap between the warning and the deaths: the accountability question is who let an unapproved resort keep taking guests.

stories.label: Karachi judicial magistrate extends physical remand of anchorperson Iqrarul Hassan by 2 days
stories.summary: A Karachi magistrate extended the physical remand of TV anchor Iqrarul Hassan, held by the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency for 'anti-state, false and defamatory' content. Lead with the mechanism: Pakistan's cybercrime law lets a state agency hold a journalist in physical custody over what he broadcast — name the law, the charges, and what he reported.

stories.label: Ship attack reports near Hormuz reach record high as oil exports slow
stories.summary: The new number: at least 12 ships attacked in a single week and 22 in the first 13 days of October — already past March's record month — as the US and Iran both claim authority over the strait and two vessels hit mines this week. Lead with the tally and what it does to ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Brent crude; TASS's count is state media and must be attributed.

stories.label: Zelenskyy warns US' Russia sanctions relief could reward Putin and fuel more attacks
stories.summary: New since the waiver order: Russia struck 15 critical Ukrainian power facilities as winter approaches, Moscow welcomed Washington's easing, and Zelenskyy says the relief will pay for more strikes. Lead with the mechanism — which restrictions eased and how much oil revenue they free for the Kremlin — and who bears it: Ukrainians facing a winter without power.

stories.label: Egypt boosted by Moody's upgrade as inflation eases and investor confidence grows
stories.summary: Moody's raised Egypt's sovereign rating, citing easing inflation and resilience despite higher oil prices from the Gulf war. Lead with the decision and its mechanism — cheaper borrowing for one of the most indebted emerging markets — and ask who has paid for the stabilisation: Egyptians through subsidy cuts and a weaker pound.

stories.label: Banks could slow stablecoin growth by paying savers more, BIS paper finds
stories.summary: A Bank for International Settlements working paper finds that when banks raise deposit rates, money flows into USDT and USDC slow — so the stablecoin threat to bank deposits is partly a price banks chose not to pay savers. Lead with that mechanism and its limit (one high-rate period only).

stories.label: This Might Be the Earliest Known Spear Murder In Earth’s History
stories.summary: Archaeologists found a spear puncture in the shoulder blade of a Neanderthal who lived 75,000 years ago — possibly the earliest known evidence of one human killing another with a weapon. Lead with how the wound was read (angle, depth, healing or none) and what it says about interpersonal violence before modern humans.

stories.label: Lone, starless cloud may be a 'dark' galaxy
stories.summary: China's FAST radio telescope found a compact hydrogen cloud of about 500,000 solar masses with no stars around it — one of the strongest candidates yet for a 'dark galaxy' held together by dark matter. Lead with why a galaxy that never lit up matters for dark-matter models, and note it is an arXiv preprint, not yet peer-reviewed.

stories.label: 梁圣又掀桌了！DeepSeek新模型斩杀GPT-6，许愿式编程时代降临
stories.summary: DeepSeek shipped V4.1-Flash-1017 with open weights on HuggingFace and ModelScope: 77.0% on DeepSWE v1.1, ahead of GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5 by its own benchmarks, while cost per task fell about 60% (3.3 to 1.3 yuan). It also opened its own search and fetch APIs at 5 yuan per 1,000 calls, two days after a five-hour API outage it refunded. Lead with the price-performance gap an open-weight Chinese model keeps forcing; the benchmarks are DeepSeek's own.

stories.label: Europe Is Racing China to Dominate Industrial AI
stories.summary: China is the world's factory and its AI models nearly match the frontier, yet Europe is betting it can lead AI on the factory floor through its industrial software and machine-tool base. Lead with the concrete asset each side holds — data from production lines versus installed industrial software — and who stands to lose manufacturing jobs either way.

stories.label: Polygon Labs completes Coinme acquisition to challenge Visa and Stripe in global payments
stories.summary: Polygon Labs closed its purchase of Coinme, buying money-transmitter licences to run a regulated stablecoin payments business against Visa and Stripe, and says it will be profitable in 2027. Lead with the mechanism — a blockchain firm buying a licence rather than winning one — and note the platform is still a technical preview with few users.

stories.label: India's 'cockroach' movement founder arrested after detention
stories.summary: Delhi Police turned the preventive detention of Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke into a formal arrest on Saturday, ahead of protests demanding that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resign over voter-list revisions; AISA chief Neha Bora was detained and released, and both groups say lawyers were denied access. Lead with the arrest as the new step, and the mechanism: a youth movement targeting the electoral roll itself, and a state answering with preventive-arrest powers rather than an answer on the rolls.

stories.label: North Korea tests latest torpedo using AI -- KCNA
stories.summary: North Korea says it tested a new precision-guided torpedo that uses AI for targeting, an underwater test announced by state agency KCNA after a run of missile launches and rising border tension with the South. The claim rests on KCNA and must be attributed; the story is what an autonomous undersea weapon would mean for a peninsula where the US and South Korean navies operate, and the Shenzhen APEC window for a Trump–Kim meeting.

stories.label: Armed men abduct 20 under-training police personnel in Mastung: officials
stories.summary: Gunmen stopped a passenger van on the Quetta–Karachi Highway in Mastung and took 20 police recruits from the Kalat Police Training Centre. Lead with the number and the road: the N-25 is Balochistan's spine, and armed groups now hold it long enough to sort passengers. The mechanism is a provincial state that cannot protect its own trainees in transit, and what it means for the families and for the insurgency's leverage.

stories.label: At the UN, plans for a global coalition to attack LGBTQ+ and reproductive rights
stories.summary: Far-right activists from the US and Latin America are organising a 'pro-life, pro-family' bloc at the UN to counter the LGBTI Core Group, using the Trump administration as an anchor. The mechanism to explain: how a coalition of states is built inside the UN system, who funds and staffs it, and which governments it courts. Name the organisers and states; report it as an organising effort, not a done deal.

stories.label: Air defenses intercept nearly 3,000 Ukrainian drones heading to Moscow over week -- mayor
stories.summary: Moscow mayor Sergey Sobyanin says air defences downed 2,730 Ukrainian drones headed for the capital since last Saturday, per Russian state news agency TASS. The figure is Russia's own and must be attributed; the story is the scale — roughly 390 a day aimed at one city — and what a sustained long-range campaign on Moscow means for the war as Kyiv says it is out of Patriot interceptors and Washington eases sanctions.

stories.label: ECB's Lagarde says bond selloff will slow inflation
stories.summary: Lagarde said in Bangkok that the global bond selloff is already tightening euro-zone credit and will curb growth and inflation, while Bloomberg reports the ECB leaning toward a December rate hike. Lead with the mechanism: markets are doing part of the ECB's job, and debt-laden France pays most for it. Name the series: the ECB deposit rate, the euro, and the US 10-year Treasury yield driving the global selloff.

stories.label: IMF urges support for poorer nations facing high inflation, war spillovers
stories.summary: At the IMF meetings in Bangkok, Kristalina Georgieva said low-income countries now spend up to 14% of their revenue on debt service while the Gulf war pushes up fuel and food prices. Lead with the 14%: money that leaves for creditors instead of schools and clinics. The mechanism is a war-driven price shock landing on countries with no fiscal room, and the question is what the IMF will actually lend or restructure, not what it urges.

stories.label: CAPPA, activists, labour group reject Lagos water privatisation, metering, demand public investment
stories.summary: Lagos State is moving its water supply to long-term private concessions with prepaid meters; CAPPA and labour groups warn it will price low-income households out of water in a megacity of some 20 million. Lead with who pays: the mechanism is a concession model that recovers investment through tariffs, set against the public investment the state has not made. Name the concessions and tariffs the source gives.

stories.label: Anthropic's Claude cracks a 25-year NSA curve mystery, what it means for bitcoin
stories.summary: An Anthropic model traced where the unexplained seed numbers behind the NSA-supplied NIST elliptic curves came from, a question cryptographers including Alfred Menezes had chased for 25 years over fears of a hidden backdoor. Lead with what was found and whether it confirms or clears a backdoor; bitcoin's secp256k1 curve is unaffected. The structural point: AI is now doing original cryptanalysis on the standards that secure the internet.

stories.label: AI agents accessing corp data undetected: CERT-In
stories.summary: India's national cyber agency CERT-In warned that AI agents are reaching live corporate systems and sensitive data without authentication, and that organisations are failing to detect it. Lead with the detection gap: agents run with credentials and permissions no security team audits. Explain the mechanism (over-permissioned agents, unmonitored API access) and what CERT-In now requires of Indian firms.

stories.label: Treme Terra: um Data Center chegando à Amazônia
stories.summary: The Amazon's first AI data center is going up in Belém without an environmental licence, and residents already complain of noise. Lead with the missing licence: who is building it, for which clients, and which agency waived or skipped review. The structural point is the AI build-out reaching the rainforest's largest city — power, water and noise borne by the neighbourhood, compute exported.

stories.label: Young children prefer to learn from and befriend strivers rather than endowed individuals - Communications Psychology
stories.summary: A peer-reviewed study finds young children would rather learn from and befriend people who succeed through effort than people born with talent or advantage. Lead with the finding and the ages tested; explain the experimental design and what it suggests about how children judge whom to trust — a counter to the assumption that children simply follow the most capable.

stories.label: Trump waives several Russian sanctions as new US law takes effect
stories.summary: Trump signed a Russia sanctions law and then, by executive order the same day it took effect, suspended its measures 'until further notice' from him or Rubio. Lead with the mechanism: a waiver clause turns a congressional mandate into a presidential option, so Congress's leverage over the war goes back to the White House. Name the lawmakers, Republicans among them, calling it craven, and tie it to the shadow-fleet tanker easing we flagged and to the Polymarket odds of Russia-Ukraine peace talks by Nov 30, which fell from 50% to 19% this week (Putin said the same day that the 'security zone' Russia is building inside Ukraine is non-negotiable). Russian state agency TASS broke it; BBC, Al Jazeera and Ukrainska Pravda corroborate.

stories.label: Brazil's Amazon deforestation hits lowest level on record
stories.summary: Amazon clearance fell 42% in a year, to the lowest since records began in 1988. Lead with the number, then the mechanism: what enforcement changed (IBAMA fines, embargoes, credit rules) and whether the drop holds against land-grabbers and ranchers. The stakes are the runoff: the record lands days before Lula faces Flávio Bolsonaro, whose father's government saw clearance surge. Datelined Brasília.

stories.label: «Coordenadas de la impunidad»: en Honduras el poder sobre las alcaldías se disputa, se hereda o nunca se entrega
stories.summary: A Contracorriente data investigation found 19 Honduran mayors prosecuted between 2015 and 2025 across 13 departments, with drug seizures and 468.7 million lempiras in audited losses; municipal power is fought over, passed down within families, or never handed over. Lead with the 19 and the pattern: the town hall is where organised crime meets the state, prosecutions end in acquittal, and the last election in Talanga produced two declared winners. The story is systemic, not one case, and shares only a theme with yesterday's Ardón story. Datelined Tegucigalpa.

stories.label: IRGC says tanker passing Hormuz through 'prohibited' route hits mine
stories.summary: Iran's IRGC navy says a supertanker carrying over 2 million barrels of crude struck a sea mine after crossing the Strait of Hormuz by a 'prohibited' route with its tracking switched off. Attribute the claim to the IRGC and say what is independently confirmed (ship name, flag, damage, any spill). Lead with the mechanism: Iran is enforcing its closure of Hormuz with mines and a lane only it permits, so every cargo now pays for war-risk insurance. Name the series: ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Brent crude. Follows the two sinkings near Hormuz and Hatami's 'closed until rights are respected' line.

stories.label: Jio's $3.2 Billion IPO Tests Ambani Appeal With Young Indians
stories.summary: Reliance's Jio Platforms is floating $3.2 billion of shares and has drawn about Rs 2.5 lakh crore of demand, with GIC, Norges, ADIA and QIA among the interested investors. Lead with who owns India's telecom backbone after the float: Gulf and Asian sovereign funds buy into the network that carries most Indian mobile data while the Ambanis keep control. The mechanism: a retail-heavy IPO that tests whether a new generation of Indian savers will trust the family that taught their parents to buy shares. Datelined Mumbai.

stories.label: Striking unions at Antofagasta's Centinela copper mine reach preliminary deal, ending strike
stories.summary: Two unions at Antofagasta's Centinela mine in Chile's Atacama agreed a preliminary contract, ending a strike of more than a week. Lead with what the workers won and what the stoppage cost in lost output, then the stakes: Chile mines about a quarter of the world's copper, and in a market squeezed by the energy-transition demand the World Bank flagged, one mine's strike moves the price. Name the series: copper. Datelined Santiago.

stories.label: China Plans AI Export Curbs To Exert Control Over Key Tech
stories.summary: Beijing proposed adding advanced AI technologies, models and chip designs among them, to its export-control list. Lead with the reversal: the country Washington spent years cutting off from AI chips is now restricting outbound AI transfers, a sign Chinese labs believe they have something worth guarding after closing the gap this summer. Explain what the list covers, who needs a licence, and who loses access (Global South buyers of Chinese open models). Datelined Beijing.

stories.label: 投影仪半年少卖70万台，都怪红果短剧太上头
stories.summary: China sold 700,000 fewer home projectors in half a year, and TMTPost traces the drop to ByteDance's free Hongguo short-drama app pulling viewers onto their phones. Lead with the 700,000 and the mechanism: a free, ad-funded vertical-video format is eating a hardware category, the same attention shift squeezing TV makers and streamers. Tell it from inside China's consumer-tech market, using the brands and sales figures the piece cites. Datelined Beijing.

stories.label: Satoshi-era bitcoin faces a bigger quantum threat after Google's new Willow breakthrough
stories.summary: Google says its Willow chip cut errors about 40-fold in producing 'magic states', the resource a fault-tolerant quantum computer needs to run Shor's algorithm. Lead with the finding and its honest limit: it does not make an attack 40 times cheaper, but it advances the method toward the ~500,000 reliable magic states per second that one modelled attack on bitcoin keys requires. The most exposed coins are Satoshi-era addresses whose public keys are already on-chain. Name the series: bitcoin. Distinct from last week's quantum-alliance count of vulnerable coins: this is the hardware result.

stories.label: Political violence: How justifications influence voter approval
stories.summary: A Journal of Politics study (Daxecker, Max Planck Institute Göttingen; Prasad, University of Amsterdam) finds that framing political violence as a justified response to an out-group's threat raises voter approval of the violence and of the party behind it. Among BJP supporters it went further: they approved less of a peaceful response by their own party. Lead with that finding: a justification narrative doesn't only excuse violence, it penalises restraint. Timely against India's crackdown on the Cockroach protests and Rajnath Singh's 'regime change' rhetoric.
